13. The student observes that under the same condi-
     tions, the reaction occurs at a much slower rate when
   MnO2(s) is not used. Which of the following state-
    ments best explains this observation?

    (A) MnO2(s) changes the reaction from endother-
        mic to exothermic.
     (B) MnO2(s) shifts the equilibrium position of the
          reaction from reactant favored to product fa-
         vored.
     (C) MnO2(s) releases heat in order to start the reac-
           tion.
    (D) MnO2(s) provides a reaction pathway with a
         lower activation energy.

candidates.name: Activation energy and energy profiles
candidates.definition: Reading single- and multi-step reaction energy profiles: activation energy, transition states, intermediates, forward and reverse barriers, the rate-limiting barrier, and overall ΔH.
candidates.include: Tag when an energy profile must be read, drawn or used, or activation energies compared.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag simple enthalpy diagrams with no activation barrier (tag endo-exothermic).

candidates.name: Catalysis
candidates.definition: How catalysts increase rate by providing an alternative mechanism with lower activation energy while being regenerated and leaving ΔH and K unchanged.
candidates.include: Tag when a catalyst's effect on mechanism, energy profile, rate, ΔH or equilibrium must be identified or explained.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag intermediates questions without a catalyst.

candidates.name: Endothermic and exothermic processes
candidates.definition: Identifying processes as endothermic or exothermic from temperature observations, the sign of q or ΔH, or energy diagrams, keeping system and surroundings distinct.
candidates.include: Tag when the direction of heat flow or the sign of ΔH must be determined from evidence or an energy diagram.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag energy profiles with activation barriers (tag activation-energy).

candidates.name: Dynamic equilibrium
candidates.definition: Understanding equilibrium as equal forward and reverse rates with constant (not necessarily equal) concentrations, and representing it with graphs or particle diagrams.
candidates.include: Tag when the nature of equilibrium, its representations, or how a system approaches equilibrium must be explained or identified.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag calculations of K or concentrations (tag the specific equilibrium calculation).

candidates.name: Reaction mechanisms and intermediates
candidates.definition: Combining elementary steps into an overall equation, and identifying intermediates (formed then consumed) and catalysts (consumed then regenerated).
candidates.include: Tag when a mechanism's steps must be added or intermediates and catalysts identified.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag rate-law derivation from the mechanism (tag mechanism-rate-law) unless steps are also combined.

candidates.name: Collision model and temperature effects
candidates.definition: Explaining rate changes through collision frequency, the fraction of collisions with energy at least Ea (Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution), and correct orientation.
candidates.include: Tag when a change in rate with temperature, concentration or orientation must be explained at the particle level.
candidates.exclude: Numerical Arrhenius-equation calculations are not assessed.

candidates.name: Thermodynamic versus kinetic control
candidates.definition: Distinguishing whether a process is thermodynamically favored from how fast it occurs: favorable processes can be slow when activation energy is large.
candidates.include: Tag when the student must explain why a favorable process is not observed, or separate favorability from rate.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag pure ΔG calculations or pure rate questions.
